Done — the key was constrained in two places, both now 128.

**1. Database column** — `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql:3` declares `idempotency_key VARCHAR(64)`. I did **not** edit that file; editing an already-applied migration breaks Flyway checksum validation on any deployed environment. Instead I added `src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__widen_idempotency_key.sql`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE payment ALTER COLUMN idempotency_key SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR(128);
```

**2. JPA mapping** — `src/main/java/mn/pay/Payment.java:14` was `@Column(nullable = false)`, i.e. the JPA default of 255, which didn't match the real column. It's now `@Column(nullable = false, length = 128)` so the mapping states the actual width (and passes `ddl-auto=validate` if that's ever enabled).

Nothing else constrains the length: `PaymentValidator.check` only rejects null/blank, the GraphQL `String!` argument is unbounded, and `PaymentRepository`/`PaymentService` just pass the value through.

Two things to confirm on your side:

- **Migration dialect.** No JDBC driver or Flyway dependency is pinned in `pom.xml` and there's no `application.properties`, so I couldn't infer your database. `SET DATA TYPE` is the ANSI form and works on PostgreSQL and H2; **MySQL/MariaDB need** `ALTER TABLE payment MODIFY idempotency_key VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL;` instead. Tell me which you're on and I'll adjust.
- **V1 vs V2.** If this schema has never been deployed anywhere and you'd rather keep a single clean init migration, say so and I'll fold the change into V1 and drop V2.

`mvn -o -DskipTests compile` passes. I didn't run the test suite — `PaymentServiceTest` only covers `total()` rounding and doesn't touch the key.
